summary: CropSeq AI is an agro-ecological decision support system that plans and diagnoses multi-year crop sequences to protect smallholder farmers from crop failure, soil depletion, and pest outbreaks in an unpredictable climate. Driven by farm GPS coordinates, the platform features a candidate recommender engine and a biophysical Evaluator DSS powered by NASA POWER satellite agroclimatology, ISRIC SoilGrids, and official agricultural matrices (BARC CZIS and UN FAO EcoCrop). The Evaluator rigorously audits crop rotations against real-world water balances, soil organic carbon changes, disease carryover cycles, and seasonal turnaround feasibility. Farmers, extension officers, and agronomists receive clear, evidence-based double- and triple-crop recommendations alongside diagnostic sequence scores and targeted smart swaps to eliminate catastrophic agricultural risks.
details:
CropSeq AI is an intelligent, climate-resilient decision-support platform designed to transform how smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable agrarian deltas plan their seasonal crop rotations. Built specifically around the three-season agricultural calendar (Rabi, Kharif-1, and Kharif-2 in Bangladesh), the system replaces broad, static advisories with parcel-level intelligence. Operating through an end-to-end computational pipeline, CropSeq AI begins with an adaptive conversational intake agent that extracts critical parcel constraints—including geographic coordinates, farm size, working capital, irrigation limits, and seasonal flood levels—while answering exploratory agronomic questions in plain language.

At its scientific core, CropSeq AI bridges space agency telemetry with soil-level realities. The backend, engineered with Python, FastAPI, and Pydantic schema validation, automatically fetches and harmonizes solar irradiance, precipitation, temperature patterns, and reference evapotranspiration from NASA POWER and Open-Meteo, alongside digital soil profiles (topsoil pH, texture, and organic carbon) from ISRIC SoilGrids. These remote-sensing layers are cross-referenced against Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) suitability databases, ensuring that candidate crops respect regional agro-ecological zones and biological succession rules, such as pest-disease breaks and legume-induced nitrogen fixation.

CropSeq AI’s primary mathematical innovation lies in rejecting arbitrary single-crop predictions in favor of multi-objective Pareto optimization. The engine simultaneously optimizes across three competing priorities: maximizing gross financial margins, minimizing seasonal irrigation demand, and maximizing soil organic health. Rather than dictating choices to the farmer, it presents the non-dominated Pareto frontier, honoring human agency. Through a modern React and TypeScript frontend, the system translates dense satellite matrices and complex trade-off curves into a clean, jargon-free Seasonal Planting Journey, accompanied by visual progress gauges and accessible rationale that bridges the digital divide for rural communities.

Our team grounded the entire architecture in the specific ecological realities of South Asian river basins. Crucially, the model accounts for seasonal land inundation levels (from Highland down to Very Lowland) to ensure vulnerable crops are never planted during monsoon submersion periods. It directly responds to the acute groundwater crisis in northern Bangladesh (such as the drought-prone Barind Tract) by heavily penalizing water-intensive monocultures in favor of drought-tolerant, soil-enriching pulses and oilseeds. Furthermore, it enforces hard budget ceilings so that every recommended crop sequence is financially achievable within a family's available working capital.

The ultimate impact of CropSeq AI is the elevation of smallholder livelihoods from fragile subsistence to regenerative, climate-proof stewardship. By replacing water-exhaustive practices with balanced crop sequences, CropSeq AI saves tens of thousands of cubic meters of groundwater per hectare, restores natural soil fertility without over-reliance on synthetic fertilizers, and cushions smallholder households against sudden climate shocks. Conceived for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, CropSeq AI establishes a scalable, open blueprint for data-driven, climate-smart agriculture across vulnerable river deltas worldwide.
